Andromeda in 2022

It's pretty good. Downloaded some mods, gave it a chance, and I'm pretty happy.
Runs waaayyy better than ME 1-3, plays better, looks 1000x better with the mods and re-shade (only about 100mb of Andromeda mods versus 50gb of ME 1-3 mods and it still looks better). Story is nothing amazing but neither were the originals.

Give it a go on sale and use the Cinematic Re-shade mod on Nexus. And have fun out there Pathfinder!

THIS IS NOT A GATEWAY TO THE MASS EFFECT FRANCHISE !!! If you haven't played the original trilogy just get Legendary Edition instead. That said, if you already are a fan and wondering if this pile of garbage is worth the trouble in 2022, well yes it absolutely is - because they've announced that a sequel is in development and like any mass effect fanatic you'll probably end up playing this anyway, so might as well do it right now while the companion app and Mass effect archives site still in functional state

Which brings us to the next point, the companion app and the site. The companion app is called apex HQ, which will allow you to play the very time consuming apex missions mini game on your mobile device making it actually enjoyable and with proper upgrades, very profitable. Mass Effect Archives is basically a Dragon Age keep for Mass effect. Login with your Origin ID, upload and review your characters blah blah blah the usual

So remember to check out those two. Get the game on sale, grab the inquisition+ andromeda bundle if you can - good deal imo. There's nothing new to add about the game itself, you've probably heard it all ( It's crap). But hey, Mass Effect will continue they said - there's still hope

PS : About the performance issues. Try turning off in game Vsync and using a third party software to lock the framerate - like afterburner or etc

If you're new to Mass Effect, then you should definitely check this game out. I played it non stop for a week. 

World exploration and the main story are a little disappointing though. I wish we can explore more. Some planets were a blast to explore but some were dull as hell. Definitely should fix some of the puzzles too, I hated the Elaaden vault, took me like 2 hours to solve.

I played my first play through heavily modded (used the guide by Synth on Nexus Mods). The mods were needed to make the game more enjoyable. The game is not on the same level as the old Mass Effect games, but still an okay play through.

This has been my third time playing the game across various platforms since its original release, and it hasn’t gotten any worse, at least.

[b]Pros[/b][list]
[*]Plenty to do
Beyond the main story there is a lot of content, like side objectives, to explore.
[*]Visuals
Environments and scenery are visually appealing, with an array of different biomes.
[/list]

[b]Cons[/b][list]
[*]Abandoned
	The game was seemingly dropped almost as soon as it was released, with no additional content and very little in the way of improvements delivered post-launch.
[*]Comparison
	This game stands on the shoulders of giants, and it does not hold up.
[/list]

[b]Story[/b]
In Mass Effect: Andromeda you play as a Pathfinder in the Andromeda Initiative, who are travelling to a new galaxy with the goal of colonising planets. Naturally things do not go as planned, when they are greeted by uninhabitable planets and hostile aliens.

I would have liked to start the story back in the Milky Way, to give us a sense of commitment from the members of the initiative. We see a lot of people who have left everything they know behind and I have to believe that cannot be an easy thing to do. There is little to show what inspired such loyalty to begin with and it would have more meaning if we saw, rather than just heard, more of why people were so committed.

The above aside, Pathfinders are a good concept. Playing that role gives you a good excuse for a ship and a crew, along with the freedom to go and do as you please. In addition, someone who is trained as a jack of all trades provides a good basis to build a character in any direction you wish. 

When it comes to new factions, the Kett are a good way of adding a diverse range of enemies, without having to create a whole race for each one, though there’s not a lot to say about them, being the largely faceless entity that they are. On the other hand, the Angara as a species are pretty disappointing. I found them far less interesting than any of the Milky Way species, so the not-insignificant amount of focus on them throughout the game was pretty tedious. Then there is the Remnant. I can’t help but feel like the abandoned technology angle has already been done with the Protheans and Reapers in the original trilogy.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2794894875 While competing directly against other antagonists in the series, like Saren, the Archon, who is shown to be a more fanatical arm of the larger Kett empire, does very little to set up any anticipation of future conflict. Of course, options were left open for expansion of the series in Andromeda, but it doesn’t suggest any larger threat, at best it is more of the same, so there wasn't much to look forward to, even if the game hadn't landed as limply as it did.

The main objective itself seemed pretty underwhelming when, like most players, the original trilogy is the obvious comparison. So thinking about the desperate race against time to stop a galaxy-wide invasion in the first game, finding the hub for some terraforming controls is hardly as dramatic, especially when there is no real sense of urgency.

[b]Gameplay[/b]
The first thing you encounter is the underwhelming character creator. Although the originals were poor, I expected a lot more from this game as it was a logical and important improvement. When it comes to faces, the majority of humanoids appear to resemble potatoes. Asari are the worst, with all of them sharing a similar face with an even more doughy appearance. For what was undeniably the race intended as eye-candy for nerds, the Asari stand out as the worst modelled species in Andromeda. I’d complain more about the lack of Asari among the leadership of the Initiative, if I wasn’t grateful for my eyes being spared from whatever went wrong there. 

Despite all of its shortcomings, the combat in Andromeda is actually quite enjoyable. The weapons are sound, with a variety of attachments to customise them as you see fit. Abilities are now a lot more versatile, being able to mix and match what powers you can use, letting you get creative and combine any powers you want. Combat itself feels more mobile, as there are more options to manipulate enemies and the battlefield, paired with the ability to jump around. The latter I was initially sceptical about, it felt wrong, but as I warmed to it, it felt less out of place.

Now, movement does leave something to be desired, as it comes across quite janky. With a controller, you have more control over the speed at which you walk, whereas on a keyboard you lurch straight into a jog, which is jarring and makes those finer movements awkward. There are some other small annoyances, such as different buttons to open and close the map; and having to hold the interact button for most things, like opening doors, which seems largely, if not entirely, unnecessary.

I have seen people call the maps too large and sparse, but I find them quite a bit smaller than the scale would lend itself to. The Kett bases are often within spitting distance of inhabited areas and even the game’s hub, the Nexus, has less explorable space than I’d expect, which is disappointing. While driving the Nomad ground vehicle, companions often engage in conversation, which breaks the silence and lets you hear how they interact with each other. The problem is, they just love pointing out enemies, so this dialogue is almost always skipped by random encounters while driving. Unless you park up as the conversation starts to hear the whole thing, it will be hard to follow, with large parts being missed.

The research and crafting system in the game rewards the player for finding what they like using and creating better versions of it, though obtaining the research necessary could get annoying. The AVP system, which allows you to unlock rewards based on your progression through the game, was an okay concept, but having to manually collect periodic resource shipments gets boring quickly.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2794894795 While it certainly gives the player more freedom in dialogue, I can’t help but feel like some big decisions lacked the weight a red or blue option brought with it.

[b]The Tempest[/b]
The ship is fine but is smaller than I would have liked. It would have been nice to see some options with it too, like upgrades tied to crew loyalty that can determine outcomes later on, like in ME2. The fact that it is completely unarmed highlights the emphasis on exploration rather than fighting which seems rather out of place in this universe.

With the Initiative it seemed like a good excuse to have more alien crew members, but no. I was never a huge fan of the human companions in the original trilogy, they just seemed boring and that was emphasised by being surrounded by a variety of interesting aliens. So, coming to Andromeda I really didn’t expect anything and yet they still proved irritating and uninteresting.

Cora may be the worst offender, acting like a vegan in that she can’t go two sentences without mentioning that she was an Asari huntress. We heard you the first seventeen times Cora, give it a rest.

The rest of the crew are pretty unremarkable, with some shallow imitations of the Normandy crew. Drack was perhaps the more promising companion. The battle-scarred old Krogan angle, which was touched on with Wrex, was pushed a bit further to create an interesting dynamic from someone who has been around over a millennium and had experienced everything the Milky Way had to offer.

[b]Now Orbiting Kadara[/b]
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2794894855 There's no shortage of content to keep you occupied. Despite this, it does also feel like things are somehow missing and as such it will be forever overshadowed by its more successful siblings. Overall, there is a lot of game here and as long as you aren’t expecting Mass Effect 4, it’s worth giving a chance.
